policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 36:13 renders the pronoun as 'Thou land art a devourer of men'. Qere אָ֑תְּ and ketiv אתי are both second-person feminine singular pronoun forms and both yield 'thou'; the verse's only textual note ('Another reading is, nations') is about the plural of גוי and does not touch this word. Nothing in the English distinguishes the readings, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV 36:13 reads 'hast been a bereaver of thy nation' — singular — which is the ketiv גויך; the mapped textual note 'Another reading is, nations' names the plural qere גּוֹיַ֖יִךְ as the alternative the ASV did not put in its text.

ASV 36:14 reads 'neither bereave thy nation any more' — singular — which is the ketiv וגויך; the mapped textual note 'Another reading is, nations' marks the plural qere וְגוֹיַ֖יִךְ as the alternative, so the main text renders the ketiv.

ASV 36:14 reads 'neither bereave thy nation any more', rendering the qere תְשַׁכְּלִי (שכל, bereave); the mapped textual note 'Another reading is, cause to stumble' names the ketiv תכשלי (כשל) as the alternative not taken in the text.

ASV 36:15 reads 'neither shalt thou cause thy nation to stumble any more' — singular — which is the ketiv וגויך; the mapped textual note 'Another reading is, nations' names the plural qere וְגוֹיַ֨יִךְ֙ as the alternative. (The other note, 'Or, proclaim against thee', is classed alternative_rendering and decides nothing.)
